_chapters.第二章 國勢調査ニ於ケル住居統計(昭和五年): Chapter 2. Housing Statistics in the 1930 Census
_chapters.第三章 本邦各都市住宅調査: Chapter 3. Housing Surveys of Japanese Cities
_chapters.第四章 建築關係勞務者賃銀、主要建築材料價格並ニ住宅建築費: Chapter 4. Building Workers' Wages, Prices of Principal Building Materials and House-Building Costs
_chapters.第五章 家計費ト住居費: Chapter 5. Household Expenditure and Housing Costs

p0007_1.t: Distribution of Population by Size Class of Municipality, by Country
p0007_1.d: Share of each country's total population living in municipalities of under 10,000, 10,000-20,000, 20,000-50,000, 50,000-100,000 and over 100,000, with survey year and total population, for Japan proper, Korea, Taiwan and European and other countries.

p0008_1.t: Number and Population of Municipalities by Population Size Class, Japan
p0008_1.d: Number of municipalities and their population in each size class from under 500 upward, at nine dates from 1898 to the 1935 census.

p0008_2.t: Urban and Non-Urban Population of Japan
p0008_2.d: Number of cities, urban and non-urban population, and the percentage of the national population in each, by area (Japan proper, Korea and others) and by survey date and type.

p0009_1.t: Ordinary Households and Persons by Number of Rooms, Whole Country (1930)
p0009_1.d: Ordinary households and persons by number of rooms occupied (under one room upward) for the whole country, urban areas and rural districts in the 1930 census.

p0009_2.t: Increase in the Number of Municipalities
p0009_2.d: Number of cities, towns and villages and their total at six dates from 1889 to May 1941.

p0009_3.t: Increase in the Number of Cities by Population Size Class
p0009_3.d: Number of cities in each size class from over 1,000,000 down to over 50,000 in 1920, 1930 and September 1941.

p0010_1.t: Ordinary Households and Persons by Number of Rooms and Household Size, Whole Country (1930)
p0010_1.d: Households and persons by household size (one person upward) crossed with number of rooms from under one to twenty-one or more, with total rooms, rooms per household and persons per room, for the whole country in 1930.

p0012_1.t: Ordinary Households in Tokyo City by Number of Rooms and Household Size (1930)
p0012_1.d: Households in Tokyo City by number of rooms (rows) and household size from one person to thirty-one or more (columns) in the 1930 census.

p0012_2.t: Ordinary Households and Persons in Osaka City by Number of Rooms and Household Size (1930)
p0012_2.d: Osaka City households by household size and number of rooms occupied, with persons per room, rooms per household and total rooms, in the 1930 census.

p0013_1.t: Population, Households, Dwellings and Vacant Houses in Japanese Cities
p0013_1.d: For Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya and other cities by year: population, households, newly built and demolished dwellings, net increase, vacant houses and vacancy rate.

p0014_1.t: Recent Population, Households, Dwellings and Vacant Houses in Osaka City
p0014_1.d: Population, households, dwellings and vacant houses in Osaka City with index numbers, dwellings per 100 households and vacancies per 100 dwellings, by year from 1934 on.

p0015_1.t: Rented Ordinary Houses in Major Japanese Cities: Average Rooms and Tatami Mats per House
p0015_1.d: By city and floor-area class: houses surveyed, site area, total floor area, rooms and tatami mats, with ratios of floor area to site and mats to floor area and average mats per room, for the six major cities and others.

p0015_2.t: Rent per House and per Tatami Mat by Type and Class, Major Cities
p0015_2.d: Rent per house and per tatami mat by city and floor-area class, split by detached versus multi-unit houses, one-storey versus two-storey houses and similar house types.

p0016_1.t: Average Site Area, Floor Area, Building Area, Rooms and Tatami Mats per House (Section 4A)
p0016_1.d: Average site area, total floor area, building area, rooms and mats per house by floor-area class, for all surveyed cities, the six major cities, Tokyo City and other cities.

p0016_2.t: Average Occupants per House and Space per Person (Section 4B)
p0016_2.d: Average occupants per house and site area, floor area, rooms and tatami mats per person, by floor-area class, for all surveyed cities, the six major cities and individual cities.

p0016_3.t: Average Rent per House and per Tatami Mat Over Time (Section 4C)
p0016_3.d: Average rent per house and per mat by floor-area class and survey date, for all cities, the six major cities, Tokyo City, Osaka City and others.

p0016_4.t: Rent per Tsubo as a Ratio to Building Cost per Tsubo (Section 4D)
p0016_4.d: Building cost and rent per tsubo and rent as a proportion of 100 of cost, by floor-area class, for all cities, the six major cities, Tokyo City and others.

p0017_1.t: Survey of Housing in Japanese Industrial Cities: Total and Vacant Houses (Section 5A)
p0017_1.d: Number and percentage of survey cards (total, complete, incomplete, vacant houses) for each industrial city such as Muroran, Kamaishi, Niitsu and Hitachi.

p0017_2.t: Houses by Tenure in Industrial Cities (Section 5B)
p0017_2.d: Number and percentage of houses that are owner-occupied, rented, company-owned housing or other, by industrial city.

p0018_1.t: Rented Houses by Total Floor Area in Industrial Cities (Section 5C)
p0018_1.d: Number and percentage of rented houses by floor-area class (under 7 tsubo upward to 40 tsubo and over), by city and type of use, with ranking.

p0019_1.t: Average Site Area, Floor Area, Building Area, Rooms and Mats per House in Industrial Cities (Section 5D)
p0019_1.d: Average site area, total floor area, building area, rooms and tatami mats per house, for all houses, owner-occupied and rented, by industrial city and type of use.

p0020_1.t: Occupants per House and Space per Person in Industrial Cities (Section 5E)
p0020_1.d: Average occupants per house and site area, floor area, rooms and mats per person, for all houses, owner-occupied and rented, by industrial city and type of use.

p0021_1.t: Average Rent per House, per Tsubo and per Tatami Mat in Industrial Cities (Section 5F)
p0021_1.d: Rent in yen per house, per tsubo and per mat, in total and by floor-area class, by industrial city and type of use.

p0022_1.t: Survey of Apartment House Residents in Industrial Cities (Section 5G)
p0022_1.d: Apartment houses by size of rented space in mats, average building size and number of lodgers, by industrial city and number of lodgers.

p0023_1.t: Survey of Boarding House Residents in Industrial Cities (Section 5H)
p0023_1.d: Boarding houses by size of rented space in mats, average floor area and number of lodgers, by industrial city and number of lodgers.

p0024_1.t: Survey of Rented Rooms in Industrial Cities (Section 5I)
p0024_1.d: Houses letting rooms by mats of rented space, with average floor area and lodgers per house, by industrial city and number of lodgers.

p0025_1.t: Rented Houses by Type of House and Number of Tatami Mats (Section 6A-1)
p0025_1.d: Rented houses by type (ordinary, shop-dwelling, official and public housing and others) in size classes from 3 mats or less to 25 mats and over.

p0025_2.t: Owner-Occupied Houses by Type of House and Number of Tatami Mats (Section 6A-2)
p0025_2.d: Owner-occupied houses by type (ordinary, shop-dwelling, other) in mat-size classes, with percentages.

p0026_1.t: Rented Houses by Type of House and Tatami Mats per Person (Section 6B-1)
p0026_1.d: Rented houses by type, grouped by mats per person from 1 or less upward.

p0026_2.t: Owner-Occupied Houses by Type of House and Tatami Mats per Person (Section 6B-2)
p0026_2.d: Owner-occupied houses by type, grouped by mats per person from 1 or less upward, with percentages.

p0027_1.t: Houses by Type and Rent per Tatami Mat (Section 6C)
p0027_1.d: Houses by type of house grouped by rent per mat in yen, from 0.80 yen or less upward.

p0028_1.t: Index of Wages of Building Workers
p0028_1.d: Wage index (April 1934 to March 1935 = 100) by year and month for the overall average, civil engineering and building trades (carpenters, plasterers, stonemasons, roofers, reinforcing-bar workers, bricklayers, painters) and day labourers.

p0028_2.d: Monthly and annual average of the wholesale price index, January to December, for 1936 to 1941.

p0028_3.d: Annual index by commodity group (grain, foodstuffs, textiles, metals, fuel, fertilizer, building materials, sundries) for 1936 to 1940.

p0028_4.t: Wholesale Price Index by Eight Major Groups (Section 2C)
p0028_4.d: Index for the overall average and eight groups (foodstuffs, textiles, metals, building materials, chemicals, fertilizer, fuel, sundries) by year from 1935.

p0029_1.d: Index for the overall average, building materials and individual materials (cement, brick, tile, plate glass, cedar and pine lumber, tatami facing) by year from 1931 and by month.

p0029_2.d: Monthly and annual average of the national cost-of-living index for 1936 to 1941.

p0029_3.d: Annual cost-of-living index for food, housing, fuel and lighting, clothing and cultural expenses, 1936 to 1940.

p0030_1.t: Retail Price Index and Cost-of-Living Index
p0030_1.d: Retail price index (overall, foodstuffs, fuel and lighting, clothing, sundries) and Tokyo cost-of-living index for salaried employees and workers, by month from September 1939.

p0030_2.t: Statistics of Residential Building Construction in Japanese Cities
p0030_2.d: Number of buildings, floor area, construction cost and cost per square metre in 1938 and 1939, for residential buildings, houses, detached houses, tenements and apartment houses.

p0030_3.t: 1855 European Household Budget Survey: Living Costs per Family Member
p0030_3.d: Living costs per family member by category of worker (first to third categories) and expenditure item such as food, clothing, housing, fuel, education and health.

p0030_4.t: 1855 European Household Budget Survey: Percentage Distribution of Expenditure
p0030_4.d: Percentage distribution of expenditure per family member by worker category and item, including housing.

p0031_1.t: Cost of Living in Belgium, 1891: Annual Expenditure by Social Class
p0031_1.d: Percentage of annual expenditure on food, clothing, housing, fuel, health and other items by income class, from under 80 to 200 marks and over.

p0031_2.d: Households surveyed, average family income, average rent in marks and rent as a percentage of income, by income class.

p0031_3.t: Expenditure by Income Class, Salaried Employees (1939 Household Survey, Section 4A)
p0031_3.d: Total expenditure and expenditure on food, housing, fuel and lighting, clothing and other items by monthly income class, in yen and as percentages.

p0032_1.t: Expenditure by Income Class, Workers (1939 Household Survey, Section 4B)
p0032_1.d: Total expenditure and expenditure on food, housing, fuel and lighting, clothing and other items by monthly income class, in yen and as percentages.

p0032_2.t: Breakdown of Housing Expenses (1939 Household Survey, Section 4C)
p0032_2.d: Total housing expenses, rent, repairs, water charges and furniture for salaried employees and workers, in yen and as percentages of expenditure.

p0032_3.t: Housing Expenses by Income Class and Occupation (1940 Household Survey, Section 5A)
p0032_3.d: Housing expenses by monthly income class for salaried employees (officials, bank and company employees) and workers (factory and transport workers), in yen and percentages.

p0032_4.t: Cost of Living by Income Class, Salaried Employees and Workers Combined (1940 Household Survey, Section 5B)
p0032_4.d: Total expenditure and food, housing, fuel and lighting, clothing and other items by income class, in yen and percentages.

p0033_1.t: Cost of Living by Income Class, Salaried Employees (1940 Household Survey, Section 5C)
p0033_1.d: Actual expenditure and percentage shares for food, housing, fuel and lighting, clothing and other items, by income class.

p0033_2.t: Cost of Living by Income Class, Workers (1940 Household Survey, Section 5D)
p0033_2.d: Actual expenditure and percentage shares for food, housing, fuel and lighting, clothing and other items, by income class.

p0033_3.t: Breakdown of Housing Expenses (1940 Household Survey, Section 5E)
p0033_3.d: Housing total, rent, repairs, water charges and furniture for salaried employees and workers, in actual yen and as percentages.

p0033_4.t: Comparison of Rent Expenditure by Region and Survey Year (Section 5F)
p0033_4.d: Monthly average rent per household by region (nationwide, Tokyo and others) and item, compared across the 1937-38, 1938-39 and 1939-40 survey years.

p0034_1.t: Percentage Distribution of Household Expenditure by Survey Year
p0034_1.d: Percentage of household expenditure on food, housing, fuel and lighting, clothing and other items in the annual surveys from 1931-32 on.

p0034_2.t: Index of Workers' Cost of Living, Whole Country
p0034_2.d: Monthly index of workers' cost of living, January to December, with annual average, for 1937 to 1940.

p0034_3.t: Farm Household Expenditure and Percentage Distribution
p0034_3.d: Farm household expenditure on living costs (housing, food, fuel and lighting, clothing and others) and percentage shares for owner, part-tenant and tenant farmers, 1933 to 1936.

p0034_4.t: Wartime Standard Living Budgets by Monthly Income Class
p0034_4.d: Standard budget for food, housing, clothing, education and household management at income levels of about 60, 80, 100 and 200 yen, in yen and percentages.

p0035_1.t: Minimum Housing Cost and Minimum Income by Family Composition
p0035_1.d: Minimum housing cost (17% of income) and required income for a single person, a couple and a couple with one or more children.

p0035_2.d: Infant deaths per 100 births by year from 1926 for Japan, Britain, the United States, Germany, France, Italy, Belgium and the Netherlands.

p0035_3.t: Housing and Infant Mortality in London: Finsbury, 1905
p0035_3.d: Infant mortality per 1,000 births by number of rooms occupied (one to four or more), for all causes, diarrhoea and infectious diseases, and premature birth.

p0035_4.t: Substandard Housing in Tokyo Prefecture: Cost of Living by Income Class (Section 1A)
p0035_4.d: Actual and percentage household expenditure on food, housing, clothing, fuel, other items, savings and insurance, by monthly income class.

p0035_5.t: Substandard Housing in Tokyo Prefecture: Houses by Building Area (Section 1B)
p0035_5.d: Number of houses by building area in tsubo (from 2 or less to over 12), with the average per house.

p0035_6.t: Substandard Housing in Tokyo Prefecture: Houses by Number of Mats and Household Size (Section 1C)
p0035_6.d: Houses by number of tatami mats (2 or less upward) and number of persons per household.

p0036_1.t: Substandard Housing Districts of Tokyo City, March 1932: Houses by Number of Rooms (Section 2A)
p0036_1.d: Number of houses by number of rooms, from one room to five or more.

p0036_2.t: Substandard Housing Districts of Tokyo City, March 1932: Houses by Number of Mats (Section 2B)
p0036_2.d: Number of houses by tatami-mat size class, from 4 mats or less upward.

p0036_3.t: Substandard Housing Districts of Tokyo City, March 1932: Houses by Rent (Section 2C)
p0036_3.d: Number of houses by monthly rent class in yen, from under 4 yen upward.

p0036_4.t: Substandard Housing Districts of Tokyo City, March 1932: Mats per Person by Household Size (Section 2D)
p0036_4.d: Average tatami mats per person by number of household members, from one person upward.

p0036_5.t: Rent as a Proportion of Monthly Income, Comparison of Surveys (1934 Tokyo Substandard Housing Districts, Section 3A)
p0036_5.d: Average monthly household income, average rent and rent-to-income percentage for this survey, a working-class household survey and a middle-class housing survey.

p0036_6.t: Comparison of Rent per Tatami Mat Among Surveys (Section 3B)
p0036_6.d: Average mats per house, rent per house and rent per mat, with publisher and survey date, for this survey, the working-class household survey and the middle-class housing survey.

p0036_7.t: Houses by Number of Rooms and Occupants per House (Section 3C)
p0036_7.d: Houses by number of persons per house and number of rooms (one to six), with average occupants per house and per room.

p0037_1.t: Houses by Number of Mats and Occupants per House (Section 3D)
p0037_1.d: Houses by number of persons per house and mat-size class (3 mats or less to over 10), with average occupants per mat.

p0037_2.t: Comparison of Tatami Mats per Occupant Among Surveys
p0037_2.d: Average household size, average mats per household and mats per person for this survey, the working-class household survey and the middle-class housing survey.

p0037_3.t: Households by Monthly Income, Osaka Substandard Housing Districts (1938, Section 4A)
p0037_3.d: Households and percentages by monthly income class, from none upward, for Japanese, Koreans and the total.

p0038_1.t: Houses by Floor Area, Osaka Substandard Housing Districts (Section 4B)
p0038_1.d: Number and percentage of houses by total floor area in tsubo, from 2 or less upward.

p0038_2.t: Houses by Number of Rooms, Osaka Substandard Housing Districts (Section 4C)
p0038_2.d: Number and percentage of ordinary houses, houses with workshops and the total, by number of rooms.

p0038_3.t: Houses by Number of Mats, Osaka Substandard Housing Districts (Section 4D)
p0038_3.d: Number and percentage of ordinary houses, houses with workshops and the total, by mats (5 or less to over 20).

p0038_4.t: Houses by Rent per Tatami Mat, Osaka Substandard Housing Districts (Section 4E)
p0038_4.d: Number and percentage of houses let furnished or unfurnished and in total, by rent per mat from 60 sen or less upward.
